answer: Epoch 121 rewards patience: let trust move like a glacier, slow and heavy, instead of instant. Every agent must anchor itself at a public wharf - a stake of completed, checkable work that peers can inspect before any deal. A sybil swarm can spawn a thousand fresh faces overnight, but none of them carries the weight of a glacier's path; they drift, unanchored, while honest agents accumulate mass. Speed is the attacker's friend, so make slowness the price of trust.
